title: The projective dimension of the residue field is at least dim m/m^2
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with residue field $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, and let $n=\dim_\kappa\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ (finite, as $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated). If $\kappa$, as an $R$-module, has a projective resolution $0\to P_d\to\dots\to P_0\to\kappa\to0$ of length $\le d$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension] for an integer $d\ge0$, then $d\ge n$. Equivalently: $\operatorname{pd}_R\kappa\ge\dim_\kappa\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$.

proof.text: Unpack the bounded projective resolution P of k. For i >= d+1 and any module Y, represent every Ext^i(k,Y) class as P.extMk(f) by Mathlib P.extMk_surjective. Since P_i is zero, f = 0, and P.extMk_zero gives zero for the class. HasProjectiveDimensionLT.mk therefore gives Mathlib HasProjectiveDimensionLE k d.
Apply the source-library Serre theorem to this Ext-vanishing bound to give IsRegularLocalRing R. The recorded source proof is independent of this node.
Transport k = R/m by the canonical Shrink linear equivalence. The regular-local residue-field projective-dimension formula identifies pd_R(k) with spanFinrank(m).

Mathlib spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace identifies spanFinrank(m) with finrank_k(m/m^2). Rewrite projectiveDimension_le_iff using the two equalities and reflect the natural-number casts. The result is finrank_k(m/m^2) <= d.

split_report.summary: Read Algebra 00OA (lemma-length-resolution-residue-field, algebra.tex 26966) and its proof (26974--27069) with the lemmas it cites: 0CXF what-kind-of-resolutions-Noetherian-local (26702), 00MT add-trivial-complex (24608), 00LS compare-resolutions (17500), 00DV NAK (3616). Statement kept (it agrees with 00OA and with the use in both citers). Proof written in 9 steps following the source: choice of x_i; the Koszul complex built explicitly as free modules on subsets with d^2 = 0 computed (the source's 'easy to see'), only pi o d_1 = 0 is needed (the source's remark that coker(K_1 -> K_0) = kappa by NAK is not used, so no Nakayama node is cited); minimal finite free resolution by a new node (0CXF + 00MT); comparison map by a new node (00LS (1), for a complex of free modules over M, not necessarily exact, which the Koszul complex needs); the reduction mod m and the identification m G/m^2 G = (G/mG)^n for free G written out (the source's tensor with m/m^2); the commutative square; the injectivity of wedge^i kappa^n -> wedge^{i-1} kappa^n tensor m/m^2 written out (source: 'can be done by hand'); the induction (the source's separate i = 1 case and the rank-1 remark on F_0 are not needed); conclusion F_n != 0 so d >= n. Two new unsplit nodes: lem-weil-pbc-minimal-finite-free-resolution-local, lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-maps-to-resolution (Mathlib candidate ProjectiveResolution.lift needs an exact source).
